rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with an expanded blastocyst and acknowledges image limitations, but it overstates confidence in identifying a clear blastocoel, ICM, and cohesive TE from a somewhat blurry image and adds subtle features like granularity/debris that are not reliably assessable.
Thoroughly integrates age, diminished ovarian reserve, first-cycle status, sperm parameters, endometrium, BMI, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with probability estimates tied to embryo quality and patient factors; minor issues include somewhat speculative adjustments and overinterpretation of reserve effects on single-embryo implantation.

Mostly aligned on SET and general prognosis, but includes several recommendations with weaker guideline support or controversial use in routine care (ERA, growth hormone, DHEA, TESE-ICSI for DFI, luteal GnRH agonist rescue framed broadly).

Provides clear next-step recommendations for transfer management and future planning, including SET, luteal support, counseling, and options if unsuccessful; slightly reduced by inclusion of some less evidence-based adjuncts.
